deep.reconstruction:
This page is a preliminary lemma on convex functions. It prepares the majorization lemma attributed to H. Weyl on the next page and, in turn, the convexity inequalities for singular values and eigenvalues of compact and trace-class operators. Those inequalities feed Grothendieck's 1953 work on Fredholm determinants (previous page: genus 0 of det(1-zu) for trace-class u).

Setting: f is convex on an open convex set U ⊂ R^n. G_f = {(x,y) : x ∈ U, y > f(x)} is the strict epigraph. It is convex, and open because a convex function on an open set of R^n is continuous.

Take a ∈ U and b = f(a), and let H be a hyperplane through (a,b) that does not meet G_f. Such an H exists by Hahn–Banach / supporting hyperplane separation. The page states four claims:

1) H is non-vertical, i.e. it does not contain the line x = a. This holds because a is interior to U, so a vertical hyperplane through (a,b) would cut G_f. Hence H is the graph of an affine function y = L_a(x) = b + Σ c_i (x_i - a_i).

2) f(x) ≥ L_a(x) for all x ∈ U. G_f is connected and misses H, so it lies in one open half-space. That half-space must be {y > L(x)}, since G_f contains points (a, b+t) with t > 0.

3) f = sup_a L_a on U, with the sup attained at a = x. Conversely, a sup of affine functions is convex.

4) If f is increasing in each variable, every supporting affine function has c_i ≥ 0. Suppose c_1 < 0 and take x_1 < a_1 close to a_1. Monotonicity gives f(x_1, a_2, …, a_n) ≤ f(a) = b. But f ≥ L and L(x_1, a_2, …) = b + c_1(x_1 - a_1) > b, a contradiction.

Purpose: in the Weyl lemma (case a, φ convex symmetric and increasing), one writes φ as a sup of affine functions with nonnegative coefficients. This reduces φ(α) ≤ φ(β) to the linear inequality Σ c_i α_i ≤ Σ c_i β_i, which follows by Abel summation from the partial-sum majorization.
errors: Claim 3 is written 'pour tout x ∈ E'; it should be x ∈ U, with a ranging over U.
The non-verticality in (1) is asserted with only a parenthetical justification. It is correct because a is interior to U.
Existence of the supporting hyperplane H is taken for granted. This is standard (Hahn–Banach / Minkowski).

ideas.what: Existence of non-vertical supporting hyperplanes to the epigraph of a convex function at interior points; convex f equals the sup of its affine minorants (attained).
ideas.modern_name: Supporting hyperplane theorem / subgradient existence; Fenchel–Moreau representation for finite convex functions
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) where Weyl-type inequalities are used

ideas.what: The subgradients of a coordinatewise increasing convex function have nonnegative components.
ideas.modern_name: Monotone convex functions have nonnegative subgradients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used in Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya and Weyl (1949) majorization arguments

ideas.what: Preparation for the Weyl majorization lemma (weak majorization plus a convex, increasing, symmetric φ gives φ(α) ≤ φ(β)).

deep.surprise_reason: Standard convex-analysis lemma (supporting hyperplanes, sup of affine minorants, monotone case) written out as a step toward Weyl's majorization inequality. It is correct and routine, with nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Claim 3: 'pour tout x ∈ E' should be read as x ∈ U (the page's own usage elsewhere).

End of point 4: the contradiction reads as 'L(x_1, a_2, …, a_n) fonction affine décroissante en x_1', with f(x_1, a_2, …) ≤ f(a) for x_1 < a_1 near a_1. The final words are best read as 'on aurait f(x_1) ≤ f(a) < L(x_1)' rather than 'f(x_1) ≤ f(a) ≤ f(a_1)'.
First line: plausibly 'f fonction convexe sur l'ouvert convexe U' (the 'ouvert' reading is consistent with the argument).
